lineage_rule: A calculated fact's citations are one Citation per (source, page): the first quote on that page among the citations of the facts in its derives_from list, in that order (rulings stage2 round 3 item 3; round 5 item 17), where an own fact contributes its own (transitively CP-1) citations; analyst inputs and CP-2A watch levels carry none. A known fact never derives from a fact that is not known (asserted by the builder). A copied upstream cell keeps the upstream fact's value_class (analyst_judgment, calculated, or None for the CP-2A definition constants) and carries a calculation_id only when calculated. A T2H cell that restates a CP-1 fact (T2H.2 copies, T2H.4 and T2H.5 openings, T2H.2 recomputed ratios) is this module's own calculated fact with cp1:<metric> lineage and calc:<fact_id>; it does not keep CP-1's class (calculated or source): only cp1_references carry the CP-1 fact verbatim with its class. A copy of a CP-2A cell in T2H.7 (level, static_decline) lists the CP-2A fact it copies in derives_from whatever the cell's class; the base_first and down_first texts of a CP-2A row list cp2a:T2B.6.<row>.level; the downside EBITDA (T2H.4) and interest (T2H.5) cells list the CP-2A shock fact they apply (D3 proof, ruling H1).
references_rule: cp1_references, cp2a_references and cp1d_references carry the upstream facts verbatim under their own fact ids with their own value_class, status and limitation; prose and T2H.2 reference them ({<fact_id>|<unit>}). No CP-2G table or claim stores a spelled upstream figure.

own_limitations: Driver values are analyst assumptions without a source citation; no management guidance or consensus is an input.
The forecast is annual over three years from the CP-1 twelve-month base; no quarterly path is modelled.
Cash interest is the analyst's rate applied to the opening debt balance; no hedging, floor or reference-rate curve is modelled.
Cash taxes and working capital are modelled together as a share of revenue; no tax shield or working-capital cycle is modelled.

No new borrowing, refinancing or covenant waiver is modelled: debt moves only by the analyst's repayments, and cash is not floored, so a negative cash balance is an unfunded requirement, not a forecast of events.
The downside applies CP-2A's settled scenario shocks to every forecast year and holds revenue, capital expenditure, distributions and repayments at the base case; no mitigating action is modelled.
The break tests reuse CP-2A's levels, which are watch levels and definitions, not covenant tests; covenant compliance belongs to CP-4.
Accessible liquidity is closing cash plus CP-1's undrawn revolver; restricted, trapped or operationally required cash is not separated.
Debt maturities and refinancing feasibility are not modelled; the maturity wall and funding gap belong to CP-2D and CP-3C.
CP-1D (earnings quality) is bound but blocked, so starting leverage is not restated on evidence-supported EBITDA and no comparison with it is made.
Minimum liquidity is an analyst assumption, not a source figure.
In the downside case closing cash is negative from FY2027: an unfunded requirement, not a forecast of events.
Gap (Material): No management guidance, consensus or covenant document is an input to the forecast.

own_limitations: Driver values are analyst assumptions without a source citation; no management guidance or consensus is an input.
The forecast is annual over three years from the CP-1 twelve-month base; no quarterly path is modelled.
Cash interest is the analyst's rate applied to the opening debt balance; no hedging, floor or reference-rate curve is modelled.
Cash taxes and working capital are modelled together as a share of revenue; no tax shield or working-capital cycle is modelled.

No new borrowing, refinancing or covenant waiver is modelled: debt moves only by the analyst's repayments, and cash is not floored, so a negative cash balance is an unfunded requirement, not a forecast of events.
The downside applies CP-2A's settled scenario shocks to every forecast year and holds revenue, capital expenditure, distributions and repayments at the base case; no mitigating action is modelled.
The break tests reuse CP-2A's levels, which are watch levels and definitions, not covenant tests; covenant compliance belongs to CP-4.
Accessible liquidity is closing cash plus CP-1's undrawn revolver; restricted, trapped or operationally required cash is not separated.
Debt maturities and refinancing feasibility are not modelled; the maturity wall and funding gap belong to CP-2D and CP-3C.
CP-1D (earnings quality) is not part of this run, so starting leverage is not restated on evidence-supported EBITDA and no comparison with it is made.
Minimum liquidity is an analyst assumption, not a source figure.
In the downside case closing cash is negative from FY2026: an unfunded requirement, not a forecast of events.
A break test whose metric is not calculable in a forecast year is missing, with the reason, when no earlier year has met it.
A leverage trajectory that cannot be calculated is missing, with the reason, not a known text.
Gap (Material): No management guidance, consensus or covenant document is an input to the forecast.

own_limitations: Driver values are analyst assumptions without a source citation; no management guidance or consensus is an input.
The forecast is annual over three years from the CP-1 twelve-month base; no quarterly path is modelled.
Cash interest is the analyst's rate applied to the opening debt balance; no hedging, floor or reference-rate curve is modelled.
Cash taxes and working capital are modelled together as a share of revenue; no tax shield or working-capital cycle is modelled.

No new borrowing, refinancing or covenant waiver is modelled: debt moves only by the analyst's repayments, and cash is not floored, so a negative cash balance is an unfunded requirement, not a forecast of events.
The downside applies CP-2A's settled scenario shocks to every forecast year and holds revenue, capital expenditure, distributions and repayments at the base case; no mitigating action is modelled.
The break tests reuse CP-2A's levels, which are watch levels and definitions, not covenant tests; covenant compliance belongs to CP-4.
Accessible liquidity is closing cash plus CP-1's undrawn revolver; restricted, trapped or operationally required cash is not separated.
Debt maturities and refinancing feasibility are not modelled; the maturity wall and funding gap belong to CP-2D and CP-3C.
CP-1D (earnings quality) is not part of this run, so starting leverage is not restated on evidence-supported EBITDA and no comparison with it is made.
Minimum liquidity was not assessed, so the liquidity break test and liquidity headroom are not calculated.
CP-2A stressed the base period Q3 25: 2025-07-01 to 2025-09-30; its required declines are shown for reference and are not comparable with the twelve-month forward path.

The metric named for CP-2A break b03 could not be checked against its CP-2A required decline: CP-2A stressed a different base period from the twelve-month base, so its required decline is not comparable.
In the downside case closing cash is negative from FY2027: an unfunded requirement, not a forecast of events.
A break test whose metric is not calculable in a forecast year is missing, with the reason, when no earlier year has met it.
Gap (Material): Earnings quality and minimum liquidity are not inputs to the forecast.

recipe: 1. Copy the closed positive store directory (blobs, snapshots, current, audit) to a scratch path.

2. Load the CP-2G head's result Module; replace only the text of fact T2H.7.b03.down_first (its shown spelling is that text); leave every other fact (including T2H.7.b03.base_first and every other row), table, claim (T2H.7.down included) and limitation unchanged.
3. Serialise the forged Module as Execution._store does (model_dump_json); its sha256 R2 must equal Module.content_hash(); write blobs/R2.

4. Build a new ExecutionSnapshot equal to the current one with the CP-2G Attempt.result_sha256 and Head.result_sha256 set to R2 (status, inputs and commands unchanged, so head_of(forged Module) equals the Head) and the same parent; write snapshots/<its sha256>.json and rewrite current to that digest.

5. In the retained receipt: set the CP-2G SettledHead.result_sha256 to R2; set receipt.snapshot_sha256 and every coordinate that named the old final snapshot (the CP-2G settling OwnerSubmission.snapshot_after_sha256: owner_workflow.py _advance -> _finish_walk; its record is retained as audit/submissions/<content_hash> by _retain) to the new digest; delete audit/submissions/<old record hash> and write the edited OwnerSubmission as audit/submissions/<its content_hash> (model_dump_json bytes); rewrite audit/receipt.sha256 with the forged receipt's content_hash (S1a R3-5 and CP-3 A4 pattern: the audit file travels under its new hash).

expect.passes: everything upstream of the probe: audit inventory, blob and snapshot hashes, ancestor walk, head_of equality, begin and publication records, call and read replay, journaled-step replay (the payload and step are untouched)
